_about: Cross-country school and child-labour facts for the childworld Monte Carlo. oos_lower: adolescents out of school, % of lower-secondary age (UIS via World Bank WDI SE.SEC.UNER.LO.ZS, admin enrolment / UN population; latest year shown; Pakistan from PES 2021-22 middle level). child_labour: % of children 5-17 (ILO/UNICEF estimates as tabulated on Wikipedia 'List of countries by child labour rate'). Years differ across rows; admin-based OOS can overstate (see docs/cambodia_observation_equation.md). Composition facts, where available, are survey-based and are used as TESTS, never for matching.

age_aligned.survey: PLFS 2018/19 (household survey; work = economic activity only, household chores excluded)
age_aligned.source: UNICEF Innocenti, Child Labour and Schooling in India: A reappraisal (July 2024), Table 7 p.34 and overall table p.32
age_aligned.notes: Out of school = work only + neither (derived by us; the report does not state it). The report warns activity status is not consistent across surveys (EUS 2011/12 gives 10.7% out of school). Rows sum to 100 within rounding. Child work 5-17 in PLFS 2018/19 is 2% (5 million), report p.20.

age_aligned.survey: MICS6 2018 (child labour = ILO MICS definition: economic work hours by age band OR >=28h unpaid household services OR hazardous conditions)
age_aligned.source: UNICEF Kyrgyzstan MICS6 statistical snapshots (tables LN.6, PR3.1-PR3.3 cited there)
unresolved: Age bands behind 'primary / lower / upper secondary' follow the national school system (grades 1-4 / 5-9 / 10-11), not the model's 6-11 / 12-14 / 15-17.
MICS child labour (26.7%, 5-17) counts household chores of 28+ hours and hazardous conditions; the model counts economic work only, so 26.7 is an upper bound for the model's quantity.
The 18.0% used so far (ILO/UNICEF via a secondary page) was not found in MICS6; kept for the old matching only.

US DOL 'combining work and school 38.4%, age 7-14' (source: ILO analysis of MICS6 2018) has no definition footnote; the work definition is almost certainly the broad one, and the denominator (all 7-14s vs working 7-14s) is unconfirmed. The page also gives 34.0% working and 94.7% attending for age 5-14.

The PR3 age-by-attendance split is only in unlabelled chart bars in the snapshot (about 27% of attenders, 22% of non-attenders in child labour); not read as data. The final report table file was not fetchable from this environment.
